hypotheses.title: Multiscale, cross-potential-field edge coherence
hypotheses.signature: Gaussian scale-space edge magnitude at sigma 3 and 10 100-m cells, normalized within the footprint, with co-location and absolute gradient-orientation agreement between reduced-to-pole magnetic and isostatic-gravity fields.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: A buried or alluvium-covered fault without a young surface scarp can juxtapose contrasting magnetic susceptibility or density units; a persistent, cross-field boundary may provide subsurface structural evidence where the Quaternary-trace catalogue has no line.
hypotheses.confounders: Lithologic contacts that are not faults, magnetic remanence, survey seams and differing source depths/resolution.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: No current script derives multiscale gradient-orientation concordance across magnetic and gravity fields. Existing per-channel AUC is univariate and ridge NMS acts on the prediction surface, not on cross-physics edge features.
hypotheses.cost: medium (approximately 1-2 engineering days plus validation runtime)
hypotheses.data_gate: Uses the existing hash-pinned training-feature owner mirror; no new external data. Original competition-file provenance remains the caveat in data/manifest.json.
hypotheses.validation: knowledge/08_preregistration_H28-1.md; fresh seeds 140-149; paired comparison to B_oof + T-v2 + H27-4 r1
hypotheses.status: preregistered gate passed; +0.00295 mean paired DTI vs current OOF best (3/4 folds, 9/10 seeds; evidence/h28_1_edge_holdout.json); catalogue-internal only, no public score
hypotheses.implementation_result: Mean ΔDTI +0.0029488388 across 40 paired cells; mean baseline 0.1045377979, H28-1+T-v2+H27-4 mean 0.1074866367; one quadrant and one seed were negative. No submission written by the holdout runner.

hypotheses.title: Multiscale LiDAR scarp persistence and structural-tensor coherence
layers: 3DEP-derived 100 m bands ex_max, ex_mean, step_max, lapneg_max, lappos_max, downface_max, upface_max, cross_max, relief, coh100
hypotheses.signature: Scale persistence of short-wavelength slope/curvature edges plus local line-orientation coherence over 0.3-2 km, not a pointwise high-slope threshold.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Previously unmapped subtle scarps may be visible in bare-earth LiDAR even when absent from a legacy or Quaternary trace catalogue; continuity can suppress isolated non-tectonic relief.
hypotheses.confounders: Channels, roads, terrace risers, paleo-shorelines, landslides, mines, vegetation artifacts and tiled DEM seams.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The current OOF workflow applies one-scale ridge NMS to a classifier score; this tests terrain-scale persistence/coherence before classification. It is not the already tested isolated-dot filter.
hypotheses.cost: medium; existing derived terrain grid available, raw 1-m DEM is optional higher-cost follow-up
hypotheses.data_gate: Existing hash-pinned LiDAR descriptor raster. Official USGS 3DEP catalog page read; the local derivative remains an owner mirror.

hypotheses.title: Dilatational-strain and conductivity intersection corridors
hypotheses.signature: Joint spatial support from dilatational-strain gradients and conductive anomalies, restricted to narrow lineaments rather than broad high-value regions.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Buried, fluid-bearing or active faults can have weak surface relief but express stress concentration and conductive alteration at depth.
hypotheses.confounders: Clay caps, basin-scale conductivity, non-fault conductive alteration, strain-field smoothing and depth mismatch.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The current model uses these as individual raster features and H27-5 types known mapped faults; it does not test explicit strain-conductivity spatial conjunction for new line candidates.
hypotheses.data_gate: No new external data for first test.

hypotheses.title: Seismicity-fabric lineaments
hypotheses.signature: Directional anisotropy and line support in earthquake-density gradients, assessed across scales wider than a single hypocenter.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Linear seismicity concentrations can reveal blind active structures missing from a surface-trace database.
hypotheses.confounders: Aseismic faults, spatially variable catalog completeness, diffuse swarms, broad smoothing in the delivered density layers.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The raw earthquake channels were included in the current feature set and channel audit, but directional seismicity-fabric transforms have not been tested.
hypotheses.data_gate: No new external data for first test.

hypotheses.title: Hydrothermal observation corridors from well/spring temperatures and chemistry
layers: INGENIOUS/GDR well and spring points: temp_c, geothermquartz_c, geothermchalc_c, geothermcat_c
hypotheses.signature: Spatially coherent thermal/geochemical observations rasterized as narrow, directionally constrained corridors rather than isotropic point buffers.
hypotheses.why_missing_faults: Fault-focused discharge and hydrothermal chemistry may indicate permeable structures absent from the compiled surface-fault traces.
hypotheses.confounders: Hydrogeologic flow away from the source fault, sparse and biased sampling, duplicate station records, non-fault heat sources, and geothermometer uncertainty.
hypotheses.differs_from_repo: The point observations are not among the current 32 raster-model features; this would add independent observation-driven line evidence rather than another pixel transform or catalogue graph link.
hypotheses.cost: high; requires station deduplication, quality filters, spatial fold controls and provenance review
hypotheses.data_gate: GDR #1391 page and package listing verified; public/CC BY. Direct binary ZIP retrieval failed in this sandbox (page fetch HTTP 500; shell TLS egress failure), so a new raw package is not verified obtainable here.
